messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a cluster of OOMs on 8xA100 TP runs after the batching heuristics change. Not the usual kvcache eviction pattern. Memory graph shows a step spike during the first forward and then a ~10% higher steady usage across the run.

maria: Profiling snapshot (filtered):
```
+----------------+---------+
| region         | extraMB |
+----------------+---------+
| pre-forward    |    128  |  # staging arena growth
| nccl-allreduce |     48  |  # comm buffers / padding
| kv-cache alloc |    256  |  # shadow copy?
+----------------+---------+
```

maria: hypothesis: new batch-slicing + headsize-aligned kernel selection is triggering extra temp buffers in NCCL paths (padding/alignment), and allocator isn't reclaiming them due to fragmentation. Also possible duplicate KV cache mapping when we fall back to CPU-backed pages.

sam: Can you paste the launch config and the per-gpu peak allocs? Also which kernel variant got selected?

maria: launch: `TP=8, batch=64->sliced 8x8, seq=1024`, kernel chosen: `flash_attn_v2_aligned128` on most ranks. per-gpu peak shows +320MB vs baseline (no slicing).

jeff: Two quick checks: 1) confirm NCCL buffer alignment pad: set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME / NCCL_DEBUG to get commalloc traces. 2) check our kvcache shadowing flag — did the slicing change trigger a fallback to pinned staging? In past we've seen a ~200MB duplicate when CPU pinning ramps.

ryan: allocator angle — if staging arena grows before we've set the watermark, fragmentation prevents reuse. Try lowering arena growth factor and enabling async-free coalesce patch I landed last week. Might shave off the steady +10%.

maria: tried ryan's patch locally, reduces steady usage by ~80MB but spike still present. Enabling `NCCL_BUFF_ALIGN=64` (experiment) reduced the nccl-allreduce extraMB from 48->8. That points to padding being a big contributor.

sam: Nice; so two levers: avoid alignment-heavy kernel selection (force the non-aligned kernel for sliced cases) or change batch-slicing so head dims align naturally. Which is lower-risk?

jeff: For short term, force kernel fallback for sliced runs (runtime flag). For medium term, can we teach kernel selector to include comm-buffer cost estimate? Add heuristic: estimated pad = roundup(tensor_bytes, align) - tensor_bytes, amortized across ranks. If > threshold prefer unaligned kernel.

maria: +1 to selector change. I'll open a small PR to gate the aligned kernel for slice patterns and add a perf test. Action items: maria -> PR to prefer unaligned kernel for slicing; ryan -> adjust arena growth and land coalesce; jeff -> dump NCCL comm allocations for next run; sam -> run A/B with forced kernel fallback.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: ran 4/5 checks, next run scheduled in 30m.

maria: thanks all — will post profiling after the next job and link logs. :thumbsup:
